tip: The liker goes in the dative with нравиться (nravitsya = to like): Им (im = to them) means 'they like'. What is liked is the true subject.
заниматься (zanimatsya) takes the instrumental, not the accusative: занимался музыкой (zanimalsya muzykoy = studied music), never музыку (muzyku).
The sya ending on бреется (breyetsya = shaves) turns the action back on the doer, so he shaves himself with no separate object.
Here the sya ending means 'each other', not 'oneself': встречаемся (vstrechaemsya = we meet one another), so no extra word is needed.
по лестнице (po lestnitse = up the stairs) shows how po governs the dative for movement along a surface.
A past-tense verb plus the particle by makes the conditional 'would': Он бы помог (on by pomog = he would help), which is not about the past.
надеется на лучшее (nadeyetsya na luchsheye = hopes for the best): the verb takes na plus the accusative, not a bare object.
быть вежливым (byt vezhlivym = to be polite): a describing word after 'to be' goes in the instrumental, so not вежливый (vezhlivy).
приближается к финишу (priblizhaetsya k finishu = approaches the finish): the verb pairs with k plus the dative for what you near.
возвращаемся из отпуска (vozvrashchaemsya iz otpuska = returning from vacation): motion out of a place uses iz plus the genitive.
готовится к экзамену (gotovitsya k ekzamenu = prepares for the exam): the verb takes k plus the dative for what you prepare for.
Я бы мог приехать (ya by mog priyekhat = I could come): mog plus by softens a plain 'can' into 'could' or 'might'.
должен был позвонить (dolzhen byl pozvonit = should have called): dolzhen byl expresses past obligation, 'had to' or 'should have'.
свой (svoy = one's own) changes to match its noun: свой дом (svoy dom, m), своя машина (svoya mashina, f), своё место (svoyo mesto, n, here).
хотели бы посетить (khoteli by posetit = would like to visit): a want verb plus by becomes the polite 'would like', softer than a plain want.
стакан воды (stakan vody = a glass of water): a container word takes the genitive for its contents.
на метро (na metro = by metro): na plus the prepositional names the means of transport, so not 'on the metro'.
От станции до дома (ot stantsii do doma = from the station to home): the pair ot X do Y puts both places in the genitive.
Если бы я мог, я бы помог (esli by ya mog, ya by pomog = if I could, I would help): hypothetical conditionals put by plus past in both halves.
Передай привет (peredai privet = say hello): the set phrase literally means 'pass a greeting' and is how you send regards to someone.
Не опаздывай (ne opazdyvai = don't be late): negative commands use the imperfective verb, warning against the action in general.
удивляется результатам (udivlyaetsya rezultatam = is amazed at the results): the verb takes the dative for what surprises you.
Дом строится (dom stroitsya = the house is being built): with a non-living subject, the sya ending makes a passive, done by someone unnamed.
считается лучшим учеником (schitaetsya luchshim uchenikom = is considered the best student): the verb takes the instrumental for the label.
чтобы все могли (chtoby vse mogli = so that everyone could): with different subjects in the two clauses, chtoby takes a past-tense verb.
чтобы не проспать (chtoby ne prospat = so as not to oversleep): with one subject across both halves, chtoby takes the infinitive.
Переведи (perevedi = translate, informal) commands one friend; adding te, as in Переведите (perevedite), makes it formal or plural.
обижается (obizhaetsya = gets offended): the sya ending marks a change of state, like English 'get' plus an adjective.
справляемся с трудностями (spravlyaemsya s trudnostyami = cope with difficulties): this verb needs s plus the instrumental for what you handle.
Её зовут (yeyo zovut = literally 'they call her') is how Russian says 'her name is', with no verb 'to be named'.
